messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @kevin — high error rate detected in api-redwood-prod (5xx spikes) for 3m. See alert: https://alerts.redwood.example/alert/6789 • runbook: /runbooks/api-5xx
kevin: grabbing it. looking at traces now — starting with the prod-frontend -> model-router spans
kevin: quick note — spike started ~1753209940, traffic normal but tail latencies shot up
maria: tagging in for assistance on routing/kv cache checks
kevin: rolled a diagnostic snapshot and checked goroutine stacks. seeing repeated grpc timeouts to model-router-03
kevin: running curl against model-router-03 health:
```
$ curl -sv http://model-router-03.internal/health
* Connected to model-router-03.internal
< HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
```
kevin: adding temporary route bypass to avoid model-router-03 — switching small portion of traffic to model-router-02
priya: can we do a quick canary reroute? if successful we should mitigate impact fast
maria: yes, canary reroute + rollback of the last deploy to model-router-03 if it fails
kevin: canary applied (10% -> model-router-02). monitoring error rate.
kevin: error rate dropped to baseline within 60s after canary. continuing to ramp.
liz: documenting customer impact: support reports ~120 customer requests impacted, majority transient errors (retry resolved). Will update support ticket tracker.
support-bot: Created ticket S-24562 and linked to this thread. Affected customers: 12 with high-volume calls; first report 1753209957.
kevin: temporary mitigation success. plan: keep canary at 20% for 15m, then full traffic shift after health stable for 5m.
maria: I'll draft the post-incident notes and start RCA skeleton. Assigning maria as primary author. tagging @alex for infra timeline.
kevin: root cause looks like an nvme flake on model-router-03 leading to delayed responses and grpc timeouts; will confirm with infra logs and kernel dmesg.
alex: pulled dmesg — repeated I/O timeouts and driver resets on node model-router-03 around 1753209920. I/O errors correlate with RPC timeouts.
maria: ok — timeline and contributing factor outline: timeline, customer impact, mitigation steps, root cause (disk flake), contributing factors (no immediate degraded-host fallback, monitoring alert threshold tuned for CPU/latency but not I/O), action items.
liz: customer impact summary for docs: ~12 customers, ~120 failed requests, order of magnitude drop in successful requests for 8–12 minutes. Support is prepping outbound comms for affected enterprise customers.
kevin: moving to full traffic (100%) at 1753210360 after 10m stable at 20%. All checks green.
maria: scheduling postmortem sync — proposed 1753293600 (tomorrow 10:00 PT). Can everyone who needs to be there confirm?
priya: I can join
alex: yes
liz: yes
legal: need to review customer-facing wording before we send out any formal postmortem to external customers — cc legal
maria: noted — adding legal review step in the RCA timeline
maria: initial action items (owner — due):
- Replace disk on model-router-03 (alex) — due 1753297200
- Add degraded-host fallback policy to router (kevin) — due 1753383600
- Extend monitoring to include node I/O error rate alerts (priya) — due 1753360000
- Draft customer-facing summary and run through legal (liz, legal) — due 1753300800
kevin: adding a short-term config tweak to decrease retry depth on model-router clients to reduce queueing (will deploy asap)
priya: I'll add an eval to Redwood Optimize to surface QPS bursts tied to backend I/O; that'll help detect similar patterns earlier
maria: RCA draft will live in GH: https://github.com/redwood/rcas/tree/incident-1753210000. I'll ping when first draft is ready for review.
maria: first draft ETA 1753220800 (~3h). reviewers: @alex, @priya, @kevin. please prioritize so we can sign off and close the postmortem loop.
alex: will review after infra disk replacement verification
liz: once legal signs off on the external wording I can coordinate comms with customers and CSMs
legal: will review wording; flagging confidentiality clauses for enterprise agreements — expect comments within 24h
kevin: retrospective thought — add an automated runbook step to detect and evacuate nodes with nvme resets before they impact RPC callers
maria: logging action items in the incident tracker and will push the first draft now. Thanks all — closing incident channel for real-time ops. follow-up comments/reviews can continue in this thread.
maria: (reaction) :white_check_mark:
